title: Fail closed on ordinary skeleton resolution errors instead of malformed fallback
description:
## Summary

`SkeletonInferrer.Infer(CreatureDefinition)` wraps the whole inference in `try { ... } catch (DomainException) { return InferMalformedDefinition(definition); }` at `Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Skeleton/SkeletonInferrer.cs:20-30`. Any domain failure — not only genuinely malformed DNA — is converted into a plausible malformed-definition skeleton. Callers cannot distinguish "this DNA is malformed" from "resolution failed unexpectedly", so an ordinary resolution error silently yields an apparently valid skeleton. `SkeletonInferrer.cs:80` also contains a silent `catch (DomainException) { }`.

Related but distinct: `TSK-0093` owns malformed-definition graph mechanics; this task owns the failure-classification boundary at the skeleton inference entry point.

## Scope

- Split normal inference from explicit malformed/diagnostic inference.
- `Infer(CreatureDefinition)` must fail closed on ordinary resolution failure with a deterministic `DomainException` that names the failure; it must not route unexpected errors into `InferMalformedDefinition`.
- Keep `InferMalformedDefinition` only as an explicitly named opt-in diagnostic path (or require an explicit malformed-definition mode argument). Do not delete the diagnostic capability if editor/debug tooling uses it.
- Preserve `Infer(ResolvedCreatureSnapshot)` behaviour, which already throws on null and does not swallow.
- Remove or justify the silent `catch (DomainException) { }` at `SkeletonInferrer.cs:80`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Valid input produces byte-identical skeletons before and after the change.
- Invalid input fails loudly and deterministically on the normal API (no malformed fallback from `Infer(CreatureDefinition)`).
- An explicitly named diagnostic/malformed entry point remains available and is the only path that can return a malformed-definition skeleton.
- A test matrix proves both directions: valid DNA unchanged; invalid DNA throws on the normal path.
- No silent `catch (DomainException) { }` remains on the normal inference path.

## Validation

- Focused Unity EditMode + PlayMode skeleton-inference tests, including an invalid-DNA matrix (non-finite positions, missing parent, parent cycle, duplicate bone id).
- `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Runtime.csproj --no-restore` (0 warnings / 0 errors).
- Generation/skeleton regression tests (`GenerationIntegrityTests`, skeleton tests) remain green.

## Findings

- `docs/audits/creaturecreator-cc-audit-synthesis-26-09-12-17-34-00.md` SYN-08 (P1, confidence 0.99) and council Seat 3, which explicitly says "do not merely delete the catch; split normal inference from explicit malformed/diagnostic inference".
- `docs/audits/creaturecreator-deep-decomposition-ownership-audit-26-09-12-20-05-00.md` P1 "Skeleton inference fallback masks ordinary resolution failures".
- Independently confirmed by reading `SkeletonInferrer.cs:20-30` and `:80` in this synthesis.

## Blockers

- Call-site inventory of `SkeletonInferrer.Infer(CreatureDefinition)` is required to confirm whether any production or editor caller depends on the malformed fallback. Unity Editor was unavailable during the 2026-09-12 late synthesis.

## Next Step

Inventory call sites of `SkeletonInferrer.Infer(CreatureDefinition)` and `InferMalformedDefinition`, then implement the split with the invalid-DNA test matrix.
